The whole endpoint surface was probed live against BOTH sandbox.meshulam.co.il and secure.meshulam.co.il, using an undefined endpoint name as a negative control. The router answers an unrecognised name with the STRING "unknown method" and a real endpoint with an err OBJECT, which makes existence testable without merchant credentials. Three documented endpoints failed that test on both hosts: getTokenOnly, updatePaymentLink, updateRecurringPayment. Two live endpoints were undocumented: updateDirectDebit and createFarPaymentRequest. Prior cycles verified parameter NAMES against the docs but never asked whether the endpoint existed.

REVERTED A PRIOR CYCLE'S OWN 'FIX'. v1.2.1 declared the transactionTypes numeric value-codes (1 CC, 6 bit, 13 Apple Pay, 14 Google Pay, 15 bank transfer, 5 Pay Box) fabricated and replaced them with an index-only table. The createPaymentProcess OpenAPI schema on the official reference page declares every transactionTypes[N] as "type":"integer" with exactly those example values. Both facts are true at once: the index selects the slot AND the value is a method code, so v1.2.1 deleted real information while believing it was removing an invention. Caught this cycle only because the Independent Judge opened the cited page instead of trusting the skill's own history. Lesson: a previous cycle's CORRECTION is itself an unverified claim, and a correction that DELETES specifics deserves the same scrutiny as one that adds them.

CRITICAL: approveTransaction requires transactionId AND transactionToken. The skill and the helper script sent only transactionId, so the step the description advertises as 'the mandatory approveTransaction step that many developers miss' could never have succeeded for anyone following it. Found by walking required params incrementally and reading which field err.id 54 names next. Same defect class in getTransactionInfo (needs both), getPaymentProcessInfo (needs processToken), refundTransaction (needs transactionToken), cancelBitTransaction (keyed by processId/processToken, not transactionId at all), createTransactionWithToken (needs paymentNum).
Resolved the v1.3.0 carry: settleSuspendedTransaction is keyed by userId, not pageCode. The live docs were right and the skill was wrong.

The API answers HTTP 200 for EVERY call including failures, and the helper script piped straight to json.tool, so it exited 0 on every API error. A payments helper that cannot signal failure is worse than no helper. It now inspects the body and exits non-zero, and GROW_API_KEY (previously documented but never used) is sent as the X-API-KEY header.

Two Troubleshooting rows were confident wrong diagnoses an agent would have quoted verbatim. 'API returns 403, cause: client-side request' is wrong twice over: Grow's own error table gives 403 as 'X-API-KEY not sent', and a request carrying a browser Origin and Referer is answered normally. The real block is the absence of CORS headers, so the symptom is a CORS console error and no 403 ever appears. 'Request returns parsing error, cause: JSON content type' is also wrong: a JSON body yields err.id 707 (invalid amount) because the fields never parse, sending the developer to hunt a bug in the amount.

Added the official numeric error table from developers.grow.business/reference/errors, which the skill had never carried. It also supplies limits the skill was silent on: Bit above 3,600 NIS (271), credit minimum 3 instalments and 25 NIS (734), and paymentNum/maxPaymentNum mutual exclusion (736).

Cross-checked israeli-payment-orchestrator: its Meshulam base URLs, multipart/form-data format and userId+pageCode auth all agree with this skill. No contradiction to reconcile. Its 0.6-0.9% fee range is hedged and belongs to that skill; this skill makes no fee claim.

CARRY: the parameter sets for updateDirectDebit and createFarPaymentRequest were not established. Both are confirmed live and now named, but probing their full required-field lists was left for the next cycle.
CARRY: apisupport@grow.business is still asserted from the previous cycle and was not re-verified against a live account portal this cycle.

Expert CRITICALs addressed rather than deferred: the server callback was presented as the trust anchor while being an unauthenticated forgeable POST (webhookKey is an identifier, not a shared secret), idempotency was an unexplained UNIQUE_PER_CHARGE placeholder with the helper script omitting it entirely, and 3DS was advertised in both descriptions with zero body coverage. Two of the four could only be closed honestly by stating the boundary: what happens if approveTransaction is never called, and how the 3DS liability shift applies to a token charge, are both unverifiable without a merchant account, so the skill now says so instead of guessing.

Three response SHAPES break naive parsing and none were documented: err is an object OR the string 'unknown method'; err.id is itself an object on getTokenTransactionsByExternalIdentifiers (err.id.content holds the real message); and `status` comes back as a JSON string on some inputs and a number on others, so a strict === 1 is unsafe. The helper script had already coerced status to a string, meaning the shipped tool knew something the prose never taught.

CARRY: reconciliation and missed-webhook policy, sandbox test cards, refunding a token charge (pageCode-keyed refund vs userId-keyed charge), cancelling a Grow-managed series, the Israeli invoice-allocation regime, and whether pageField[fullName]/[phone] are genuinely required on createPaymentProcess.
